content: The test image shows a young soybean seedling stem/hypocotyl with reddish-brown discoloration and rot at the base — classic damping-off or root rot symptoms. Top candidates: Rhizoctonia, Pythium_damping_off, Phytophthora, Fusarium.

After reviewing all 8 images (test + 7 references across Rhizoctonia, Pythium_damping_off, Phytophthora, Fusarium):

**Test image analysis:**
- Young soybean seedling/hypocotyl being held at soil line
- Reddish-brown/pink coloration running along the hypocotyl
- Brown rotted tissue at the base/soil line junction
- Soil and crop residue visible in background

**Comparisons:**
- **Rhizoctonia** (Dise_18, Dise_29): Shows reddish-brown to tan/brown lesions on hypocotyl stem — Dise_29 especially shows a firm brown lesion at the node area, similar texture to the test image
- **Pythium_damping_off** (Dise_2, Dise_12, Dise_32): Shows more water-soaked collapse, pre-emergence rot, or soft decay — less firm than what the test image shows
- **Phytophthora**: Whole-plant wilting, doesn't match
- **Fusarium**: Different presentation (older plant, curled stems)

The reddish-brown firm hypocotyl discoloration with a distinct lesion at the soil line is most consistent with Rhizoctonia root rot (post-emergence damping off), which causes that characteristic reddish-brown canker on the hypocotyl.
